items.text: While alive supervision is active, when a supervised task has not completed an execution for 2 consecutive periods of its own, the software shall detect an alive fault with fault code 1 for that task.
The software shall activate alive supervision at the instant the start-up integrity checks have passed, and not before.

When a supervised task has not started by the end of its late-start limit, counted from the release of that task, the software shall detect a late-start fault with fault code 2 no later than 100 µs after the limit expires; a start delay equal to the limit counts as within the limit.

When the execution time of a supervised task, counted from the start of that execution, exceeds the execution limit of that task without a completion having been reported, the software shall detect an overrun fault with fault code 3 no later than 100 µs after the limit expires, without waiting for the task to complete; an execution time equal to the limit counts as within the limit.
The software shall measure task start delays and execution times from the timer time base with a resolution of 100 µs.
items.rationale: The timer peripheral is the time base named in CON-SUP-003; the 100 µs resolution is the measurement resolution behind the detection windows of SWR-TIM-001 and SWR-TIM-002.

items.text: At the end of each control cycle, when the checkpoints of the tasks released in that cycle have not arrived in the configured order or a checkpoint is missing, the software shall detect a flow fault with fault code 4.

Unless a watchdog reset occurs first, when a flow fault with fault code 4 is detected at the end of a control cycle, the software shall send one fault report for that control cycle whose entity is the task expected at the first position, in the configured release order of the tasks released in that cycle, at which the received checkpoint differs from the expected one or is missing.

The software shall read the set of supervised tasks, their periods, late-start limits, execution limits and checkpoint order from the configuration data block, so that changing them requires no change to the program code.
items.rationale: The configuration data block is the single block with its own stored CRC of CON-SUP-107.

items.text: The configuration data shipped with the software shall define the tasks T_IN, T_CTRL and T_OUT with a period of 10 ms, released in that order in every control cycle, and the task T_DIAG with a period of 100 ms, released after T_OUT in every tenth control cycle, with default late-start limits of 2 ms, default execution limits of 3 ms for each 10 ms task and a default execution limit of 20 ms for T_DIAG.

When the configuration data at start-up contains a timing limit longer than the period of its task, a task period of zero, or an entry naming an unknown task, the software shall detect a configuration fault with fault code 9.
items.rationale: This check is made on configuration data that has passed the integrity check of SWR-INT-002.

items.text: When a configuration fault with fault code 9 is detected, the software shall latch the safe state until a power-on reset.
During start-up, the software shall start the independent watchdog, which runs from its own clock, with a timeout of 100 ms.
items.rationale: The register values that realise the timeout are derived in the design from the reference manual (CON-SUP-106). The reset on expiry is performed by the hardware; the software obligation is the correct start and the service of SWR-WDG-005.

items.text: At the end of each control cycle, when no fault with fault code 1 to 7 or 9 has been detected since the last reset and the safe state is not latched, the software shall refresh the window watchdog once.
During start-up, the software shall configure the window watchdog so that a refresh earlier than 6 ms or later than 12 ms after the previous refresh causes a reset.
items.rationale: The register values that realise the window are derived in the design (CON-SUP-106).

items.text: From the detection of a fault with fault code 1 to 7 or 9 until the next reset, and while the safe state is latched, the software shall withhold every watchdog service action, including the refresh of the window watchdog.

While no fault with fault code 1 to 7 or 9 has been detected since the last reset and the safe state is not latched, the software shall service the independent watchdog so that the time from the reset to the first service and the time between any two consecutive services are each less than 100 ms.

Before releasing any task, the software shall detect a code integrity fault at start-up with fault code 5 when the CRC (width 32 bits) of the MPEG-2 variant (polynomial 0x04C11DB7, initial value 0xFFFFFFFF, no input or output reflection, no final XOR, computed over the bytes in increasing address order) computed over the program code between the linker symbols __app_start and __app_end differs from the reference value stored at the linker symbol __app_crc as a little-endian word of 32 bits, outside that range.

Before releasing any task, the software shall detect a configuration integrity fault with fault code 6 when the CRC (width 32 bits) of the MPEG-2 variant (polynomial 0x04C11DB7, initial value 0xFFFFFFFF, no input or output reflection, no final XOR, computed over the bytes in increasing address order) computed over the configuration data block differs from the CRC stored with that block as a little-endian word of 32 bits.

While the application runs, in each control cycle the software shall add the next 1 KiB segment of the program code to the running CRC computation, continuing from the end of the previous segment and restarting at __app_start after the last segment of a pass, a last segment shorter than 1 KiB being the remaining bytes.
items.rationale: Segment order and the restart at the end of a pass are derived from the full-pass obligation of SYS-SUP-017 and the single reference value of CON-SUP-124.

items.text: The software shall complete a full pass of the run-time program-code check of a 1 MiB image within 11 s.
items.rationale: 1 MiB at 1 KiB per control cycle of 10 ms gives 1024 cycles, which is 10.24 s, within 11 s (SWR-INT-003).

items.text: The software shall use at most 0.5 ms of processor time per control cycle for the run-time program-code check.

When the run-time program-code check completes a full pass over the program code and the CRC (width 32 bits) of the MPEG-2 variant (polynomial 0x04C11DB7, initial value 0xFFFFFFFF, no input or output reflection, no final XOR, computed over the bytes in increasing address order) it computed differs from the reference value stored at the linker symbol __app_crc as a little-endian word of 32 bits, the software shall detect a run-time code integrity fault with fault code 7.
From the start of start-up after any reset until the start-up integrity checks have passed, the software shall hold both control outputs and the status signal low.
items.rationale: Software share of SYS-SUP-020; the output level before the first software action is hardware-defined (OP-SWR-002). The software drives the levels through the GPIO driver interface.

items.text: While the start-up integrity checks have passed, no fault with fault code 1 to 7 or 9 has been detected since the last reset and the safe state is not latched, the software shall drive the status signal high.
When a fault with fault code 1 to 7 or 9 is detected, the software shall drive both control outputs low and the status signal low within 50 ms of the instant the fault becomes detectable by its rule.
items.rationale: The detectable instant is the one of CON-SUP-105 for each fault class. The whole 50 ms is taken as the software budget at the output write because the system requirement gives no hardware share; see OP-SWR-001.

items.text: While the safe state is latched, the software shall hold both control outputs and the status signal low from the start of every start-up until a power-on reset.
items.rationale: The hold during the reset itself is a hardware property (SYS-SUP-046); the software holds the levels from the start of each start-up.

items.text: When a fault with fault code 1 to 7 is detected and the detection does not latch the safe state, the software shall hold both control outputs and the status signal low from the instant of safe-state entry until the reset that follows.
Unless a watchdog reset occurs first, the software shall send the fault report on the diagnostic serial line within 10 ms of the detection of the fault.
The software shall send each fault report as the text line FLT,<code>,<entity>,<ms since start> terminated by a line feed.

The software shall assign fault codes as follows: 1 alive, 2 late start, 3 overrun, 4 flow, 5 code integrity at start-up, 6 configuration integrity, 7 code integrity at run time, 8 watchdog reset, 9 configuration out of range.

The software shall report the name of the affected task as entity for fault codes 1 to 3, the entity CODE for fault codes 5 and 7, the entity CONFIG for fault codes 6 and 9, and the entity IWDG or WWDG for fault code 8, according to the watchdog whose reset flag was set.

The software shall express <ms since start> in each fault report as the milliseconds since the latest reset of any kind, as an unsigned decimal number of 32 bits that wraps to zero after 4294967295 ms.
items.rationale: CON-SUP-126 defines unit, width, wrap and zero point (latest reset) but not the instant whose elapsed time is reported (detection, start of transmission or another); blocking open point OP-SWR-006.

items.text: When the classified reset cause is independent watchdog or window watchdog, the software shall send a fault report with fault code 8 at start-up.

When a fault with fault code 1 to 7 is detected and the detection does not latch the safe state, the software shall request a software reset within 20 ms after the later of the completion of the fault report transmission and the completion of the safe-state entry.

When a fault with fault code 1 to 8 is detected for the third consecutive time with the same fault code, with no detection of a different fault code between the first and the third detection and without 60 s of fault-free operation since the first of these detections, the software shall latch the safe state until a power-on reset.
While the safe state is latched, the software shall not request a software reset.
The software shall keep the safe-state latch, the fault history and the fault count in memory that survives software resets and watchdog resets.
items.rationale: The memory itself is a hardware element; this software requirement places the data in it. The fault count is kept with the history because SYS-SUP-033 requires it to survive software and watchdog resets.

items.text: When the classified reset cause is power-on, the software shall clear the safe-state latch, the fault history, the fault count and the repeated-fault information of SWR-SAF-007 during start-up.
items.rationale: After a loss of power the content of the retained memory is not defined by the inputs, so the software initialises it on a power-on reset.

items.text: When a fault report is sent, the software shall add that fault report to the fault history in the retained memory of SWR-SAF-004, keeping at least the 8 most recent fault reports and discarding the oldest fault report when it needs the space.
items.rationale: Derived: retaining the history (SWR-SAF-004) does not by itself supply the reports that SWR-DIA-003 returns; the history must receive each report. Order of retrieval stays OP-SWR-004.

items.text: When a fault report is sent, the software shall increase the fault count in the retained memory of SWR-SAF-004 by one.
items.rationale: Split from SWR-SAF-006; the fault count is the value returned by SWR-DIA-001.

items.text: The software shall keep in the retained memory of SWR-SAF-004 the fault code of the latest detection, the number of consecutive detections of that fault code, and the fault-free operation time elapsed since the first of these detections.
items.rationale: Derived: SWR-SAF-002 applies across resets, so the information it needs must survive them. The elapsed time is the time since the first detection of the sequence (as in SYS-SUP-028), not since the latest detection; it is advanced by SWR-SAF-011 and set by SWR-SAF-009 and SWR-SAF-012. Time while the software does not run is not counted (OP-SWR-007).

items.text: While the consecutive-detection count kept under SWR-SAF-007 is greater than zero, the software shall increase the elapsed time kept under SWR-SAF-007 by 10 ms at the end of each control cycle in which the start-up integrity checks have passed, no fault with fault code 1 to 7 or 9 has been detected since the last reset and the safe state is not latched, keeping the elapsed time unchanged in every other control cycle.
items.rationale: Derived, split from SWR-SAF-007: the 60 s of SWR-SAF-002 can only be evaluated if the elapsed time advances during fault-free operation and survives resets. The step is 1 control cycle (10 ms). Only fault-free operation counts: the time does not advance in the cycle of a detection, nor from a detection until the next reset (fault handling: report, safe-state entry, reset request), nor while the safe state is latched, nor before the start-up checks have passed; it advances again from the first cycle after the reset that follows, once the start-up checks have passed. A fault with fault code 8, reported at start-up, does not stop the counting after the start-up checks have passed. Time while the software does not run is not counted (OP-SWR-007).

items.text: When a fault with fault code 1 to 8 is detected, the kept count under SWR-SAF-007 is greater than zero, the detected fault code equals the kept fault code and the kept elapsed time is less than 60 s, the software shall increase the kept count by one.
items.rationale: Derived, split from SWR-SAF-007: the repeated-fault rule of SWR-SAF-002 needs these values current at each detection. The 60 s is measured from the first detection of the sequence, so the elapsed time is not reset by the second detection; a different fault code, or a detection after 60 s of fault-free operation since the first, starts a new sequence. A detection at exactly 60 s counts as 60 s of fault-free operation, so no latch. The elapsed time is kept unchanged on this path. The latch itself is SWR-SAF-002, which applies to the increased count; the update is made before the latch or reset request is evaluated. The other path is SWR-SAF-012.

items.text: When a fault with fault code 1 to 8 is detected and the condition of SWR-SAF-009 is not met, the software shall start a new sequence by replacing the values kept under SWR-SAF-007 with the detected fault code, a fault count of one, an elapsed time of 0 ms.
items.rationale: Derived, split from SWR-SAF-009: a different fault code, or a detection after 60 s of fault-free operation since the first, starts a new sequence of SWR-SAF-007. The update is made before the latch or reset request is evaluated.

items.text: At start-up after a software reset or a watchdog reset, the software shall continue from the values kept under SWR-SAF-007 without clearing them.
items.rationale: Derived, split from SWR-SAF-007: SWR-SAF-002 applies across resets; only a power-on reset clears the values (SWR-SAF-005).

items.text: At start-up, the software shall classify the reset cause from the reset flags as power-on, independent watchdog, window watchdog, supervisor reset or other.
At start-up, the software shall send the classified reset cause in a start-up message on the diagnostic serial line.
items.rationale: Message format is open point OP-SWR-003 (OP-SYS-005 is carried over, not closed).

items.text: When the request GET STATUS is received on the diagnostic serial line, the software shall return STS,<state>,<fault count> within 50 ms, with <state> selected as defined in SWR-DIA-002 and <fault count> the number of fault reports since the last power-on reset.

The software shall select the <state> value of STS,<state>,<fault count> as follows: LATCHED while the safe state is latched until a power-on reset; SAFE from the instant a fault with fault code 1 to 7 or 9 is detected, during start-up or in operation, until the next reset, when the safe state is not latched; STARTUP from any reset until the start-up checks have passed, when no such fault has been detected since that reset and the safe state is not latched; OPERATIONAL after the start-up checks have passed, when no such fault has been detected since the last reset and the safe state is not latched; a fault report with fault code 8 at start-up does not by itself change the state.
When the request GET FAULTS is received on the diagnostic serial line, the software shall return the last 8 fault reports within 50 ms.
items.rationale: Order and the case of fewer than 8 recorded reports are open point OP-SWR-004.

items.text: When the request GET RESET is received on the diagnostic serial line, the software shall return RST,<cause> within 50 ms, with <cause> one of POR, IWDG, WWDG, SW or OTHER, the classified reset cause.
When a request other than GET STATUS, GET FAULTS or GET RESET is received on the diagnostic serial line, the software shall answer ERR.
items.rationale: Request framing is open point OP-SWR-003.

items.text: The software shall use the diagnostic serial line at 115200 baud with 8 data bits, no parity and 1 stop bit.

The software shall use no more than 10 % of the processor time, measured as its execution time over any 1 s window in normal operation without fault and without service request on the simulator at the configured core clock.
items.rationale: Core clock value is open point OP-SWR-005 (from OP-SYS-007).

items.text: The software shall use no dynamic memory allocation and no recursion.
The software shall be written in the C programming language of the C11 edition, using no language extension that is not part of that edition.
items.rationale: Derived: CON-SUP-004 requires C11 together with the two restrictions of SWR-RES-002, but SYS-SUP-041 carries only the restrictions; this requirement carries the language constraint.

items.text: The software test build shall provide a test hook that injects each fault class with fault codes 1 to 9.
The software shall exclude the fault-injection test hooks from the production build.
The software shall run on the Renode simulator with the STM32N6 platform description, without the real board.

open_points.text: SYS-SUP-022 gives no split of the 50 ms reaction time between software and hardware output drive. SWR-OUT-003 takes the whole 50 ms for the software up to the output write, with the output drive delay taken as negligible.

The level of the control outputs and status signal between a reset and the first software action is a hardware property that the inputs do not state; SWR-OUT-001 covers only the time from the start of start-up.

Request framing (terminators, case, whitespace) for the diagnostic requests and the format of the start-up message are not decided in the inputs (carried over from OP-SYS-005, deferred to sw-req and not decidable here). The requirements are correct and verifiable at the level of the request name and the cause value.
The order of the fault reports returned by GET FAULTS, and the response when fewer than 8 reports are recorded, are not decided in the inputs.
The configured core clock value used for the processor-time measurement of SWR-RES-001 is not given (carried over from OP-SYS-007).

The event whose elapsed time <ms since start> reports is not decided: CON-SUP-126 gives only the zero point and the number format. Detection, start of transmission and completion of transmission can differ by up to 10 ms (SWR-RPT-001), so a design and a test cannot agree on one value. A product decision on the event to timestamp is needed; SWR-RPT-005 then states it.

The inputs do not say whether the time a reset takes, with the software not running, counts as fault-free operation for the 60 s of SYS-SUP-028. SWR-SAF-007 counts only the time the software runs; the effect is at most the duration of a reset.
